title: The degradation ladder
point: Under outage or overload, step down visible rungs instead of failing, record the rung on every span, and tell the user which rung they are on.
definition: The degradation ladder is an ordered set of reduced-service modes: healthy, slow, saturated, budget spent and unreachable. The system moves down one rung as conditions worsen and back up as they recover.

objective.text: Given four failure signals, order the rungs of the degradation ladder, choose the rung each signal triggers, and specify what the user sees on each.

misconceptions.claim: Graceful degradation means hiding failures from the user.
misconceptions.correction: The user is told which rung they are on. A visible notice that summaries are delayed preserves trust, while silently worse answers erode it.

misconceptions.claim: When the primary model is down, the only option is an error page.
misconceptions.correction: Rungs exist between full service and failure: queue the expensive part, route to a standby model, keep static content, or run fully offline.

l1: Rung 0 is healthy, with full features. Rung 1 is slow: queue the expensive part and show a partial result now. Rung 2 is saturated: route to a smaller or standby model with shorter output.
Rung 3 is budget spent: turn AI features off and keep static content. Rung 4 is unreachable: run fully offline or locally.
The rung is recorded on every span, and the user is always told which rung they are on.
l2: A support portal's primary model jumps from 4 seconds to 25 seconds at p95. That is rung 1: show the retrieved help articles at once and queue the drafted reply.
Later the provider starts returning rate-limit errors. That is rung 2: route to the standby model and tell users that answers are briefer for now.
At 18:00 the daily budget runs out, which is rung 3: AI features switch off, while search and the static FAQ stay up. If the network drops, rung 4 serves cached content offline.
l3: Each rung is a feature you must build and test, so the ladder carries real engineering cost.
Justify it with a number. A provider with 99.5 per cent monthly availability is down for about 3.6 hours in a 30-day month. With a working rung 2, those hours become degraded rather than dark.
Recording the rung on every span lets you measure time spent per rung. That is how you spot a system that has quietly sat on rung 2 for days.
